blocks.raw: <Tip>**Joint and several liability** means each partner can be held personally liable for the full amount of a claim, not just their proportional share. A client may pursue any single partner for the entire loss, leaving that partner to seek contribution from the others.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <ExamTip>Partnership dissolution is a common LEA topic. Key triggers: agreement of all partners, death of a partner, incapacity, or breach of partnership terms. blocks.raw: <ArticleMedia id="media-prac-frm-002-governance-comparison" layout="single" type="image" status="placeholder" alt="Three-panel organizational governance diagram: (1) Sole Proprietorship — single architect at top with 100% control, unilateral decision-making, no board or partners; (2) Partnership — all partners in governance circle, majority or unanimous decisions per agreement, profit-sharing ratios; (3) Corporation — hierarchical structure: Shareholders (75% RLA min) → Board of Directors (RLA only) → Executive Officers (RLA only) → Staff. Each panel shows: who makes strategic decisions, who has profit rights, and succession mechanism. Annotations highlighting key legal constraints: RLA majority rule (Sec. 5 RA 9266), non-architect shareholder limits." caption="Practice Form Governance — Decision-Making and Ownership Control Comparison" suggestedAsset="Architectural reference image or diagram" placementIntent="Visual reference for architectural period/typology" />
